Seems to be a `regression`, which version last worked?

> > With this new Godot 4 release, it isn't possible anymore to change focus to controls
>

Damn... It worked fine on Godot 4.3, I don't test the dev / unstable versions, so Idk...

Edit: does the 4.5 milestone means that will only be fixed on 4.5? Or there will be a 4.4.x version to fix it?

> Edit: does the 4.5 milestone means that will only be fixed on 4.5? Or there will be a 4.4.x version to fix it?


I have seen a similar question here before:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102998#issuecomment-2682242348
_(or the approach that should answer your question)_
This is a situation where the `ScrollContainer` overlaps with external controls, which is not considered in #63059.

> This is a situation where the `ScrollContainer` overlaps with external controls, which is not considered in [#63059](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/63059).

Wdym external controls? Is there a temporary solution I can do?
And wdym it's not considered?

> Wdym external controls? 

Not a descendant control of `ScrollContainer`. That is, `ScrollContainer` (sc) is not its (expected control) ancestor (the result of `sc.is_ancestor_of(expected)` is `false`).

> Is there a temporary solution I can do? 

Make their rects non-intersecting: 

For MRP, keep the center of the `ScrollContainer` unchanged, reduce its width; slightly adjust the position of the expected controls. `HBoxContainer` with `theme_override_constants/separation` should be able to help.

For your project demo video, the elements are somewhat similar, so it is visually indistinguishable which controls are outside the `ScrollContainer`.

> And wdym it's not considered?

When looking for neighbors outward from the `ScrollContainer`, some cases are simplified to looking from the border of the `ScrollContainer`, which ignores this case (it does not need to be repositioned).

The MRP has not changed, right? I remember the MRP I tested was similar to the project below. I may have mixed up the MRPs of different issues. Sorry.

[a.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19406360/a.zip)

If the `ScrollContainer` does not have `follow_focus` enabled, it should not look for focus neighbors among the shadowed descendant controls (the control that is clipped by the `ScrollContainer` and is not visually visible). Regardless of whether it is off-screen or not.

#63059 mainly fixes this situation. You can view the difference in the gif provided there. Allowing it may result in a visually visible control not having focus.

I don't understand? Is this actually a bug that needs a fix or it's just the intendent feature?

If I enable follow focus, it ruins my game's code, because then the smooth animation will look glitchy when going back with the left arrow, I've tested this before. (edit: I found a fix)

Navigation requires visual feedback. So if navigation is allowed in shadowed descendant cotrols, there is no clear visual indication unless `follow_focus` is enabled. You are not sure where you have navigated to. If there are a lot of shadowed descendant controls, users may complain that ui navigating is ineffective.

Navigation via the arrow keys relies on distance and position. Navigation via the Tab key mainly relies on the node hierarchy.  So I think allowing navigation in shadowed descendants is problematic, it's just that the use of Tab navigation is not easy to fix, and it's mostly in addition to arrow key navigation.

The Project Manager is a good example of a lack of visual feedback, although it's for different reasons: if you add a lot of projects, initially pressing the keyboard won't give you any feedback until you've pressed enough.

I just hit the same problem after recently upgrading from 4.3 to 4.4.
For my use case it is not good enough that the focused control is fully visible so I always needed custom code to scroll to the correct position (using a tween) and disabled **ScrollContainer.follow_focus**.
Of course Godot 4.4 completely broke this approach.
Without **follow_focus** I cannot select 'off-screen Controls' anymore and with it I get jumpy animations.
I could not fix this (so I am interested in what the original reporter did myself) but the ugly workaround to get it working as before is to enable **follow_focus**, undo whatever **follow_focus** does to the scroll position in **Viewport.on_gui_focus_changed()** and then let your custom code take over.
As I do not consider this a fix it should not be added to the documentation but perhaps other Godot users who stumble upon this issue may find this workaround helpful.

> [@Rindbee](https://github.com/Rindbee) Navigation requires visual feedback. So if navigation is allowed in shadowed descendant cotrols, there is no clear visual indication unless `follow_focus` is enabled. You are not sure where you have navigated to. If there are a lot of shadowed descendant controls, users may complain that ui navigating is ineffective.

Correct. But forcing this onto users and breaking perfectly fine working code is IMHO not the right decision, especially as it is nowhere mentioned as a breaking change in the 4.3 to 4.4 migration guide.
Perhaps I am doing something wrong and you could show me the way how it is done correctly.

The node structure of my UI is the following:
```
-Control
  -some stuff
  -ScrollContainer
    -VerticalContainer (larger than scroll container)
      -CustomControl1
      -CustomControl2
      ...
      -CustomControlN
```
The number of custom controls is not fixed.
Each **CustomControl** consists of multiple containers, labels, texture_rects and one or more buttons. Only the buttons can receive focus, but if any button receives focus the complete **CustomControl** needs to be visible, preferably by scrolling smoothly. As the **ScrollContainer** class cannot do this for me I need some custom code to calculate the new scroll position and tween to it.
The **CustomControl**s do not overlap (since they are inside a **VerticalContainer**).
Being able to focus controls inside the **VerticalContainer** but outside the **ScrollContainer** made it very easy to just calculate the correct scroll position and nicely animate the scrolling without interference from **follow_focus**.
Now I am forced to enable **follow_focus**, undo what it does to the scroll position and then continue as before, nullifying exactly what this new behavior was trying to achieve.
Game GUIs are different and (visually) more complex than standard application GUIs (what the editor uses). Making it harder to do the advanced stuff in order to make it easier to do the easy stuff may not be the best decision for a game engine.
But perhaps I did not set up my GUI correctly so I am interested what the correct way to achieve my goal is.

I was under the impression that disabling **follow_focus** was the way to go when doing custom scrolling and enabling it when the engine should do it automatically.
Now I am confused and would like to know what actually is **follow_focus** good for?

> Now I am confused and would like to know what actually is **follow_focus** good for?

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3e4f5480689653e21433c9766e0643bf91c00e46/doc/classes/ScrollContainer.xml#L46-L48

As the documentation states, it simply ensures that the descendant control that has **just acquired focus** appears—as fully as possible—within its visible area.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3e4f5480689653e21433c9766e0643bf91c00e46/scene/gui/scroll_container.cpp#L345-L348

Its implementation code is also very simple.  Although this method cannot be overridden directly, you can use similar logic to achieve the overwriting effect.

> Each **CustomControl** consists of multiple containers, labels, texture_rects and one or more buttons. Only the buttons can receive focus, but if any button receives focus the complete **CustomControl** needs to be visible, preferably by scrolling smoothly. 

Clearly, it does not clearly understand your intentions. Does it, then, align with the description in the documentation?

```gdscript
extends ScrollContainer

func _ready() -> void:
	get_viewport().gui_focus_changed.connect(_gui_focus_changed)

func _gui_focus_changed(control : Control) -> void:
	# Get the one you want to display when the control is focused through a NodePath or other.
	var to_display = control.get_parent_control()
	if to_display and follow_focus and is_ancestor_of(to_display):
		# Wait for the next frame to ensure that the `ensure_control_visible()` 
		# call within the native logic completes and successfully updates the cache.
		await get_tree().process_frame
		ensure_control_visible(to_display)
```
You can use the above code to achieve the effect of "overwriting" the original logic.

> As the documentation states, it simply ensures that the descendant control that has **just acquired focus** appears—as fully as possible—within its visible area.

You misunderstood me. The question was, "what is the use case of setting **follow_focus** to **false**?"

> Clearly, it does not clearly understand your intentions.

And I do not want it to do that. I just want to disable **follow_focus** and use my own scrolling code.

> Does it, then, align with the description in the documentation?

No. The documentation says nothing about **follow_focus** changing which components can be focused and which cannot. It is a breaking change and quite a strong side effect that should obviously be mentioned in the documentation.

> extends ScrollContainer
>...
> You can use the above code to achieve the effect of "overwriting" the original logic.

First of all your code makes assumptions about the layout of my CustomControl which are not true.
As I said the whole CustomControl needs to be visible not only the parent of my button, so
`var to_display: CustomControl = control.owner as CustomControl` would be correct.
Second, `ensure_control_visible()` cannot be used as I stated that I want smooth scrolling and not a harsh jump.
Just to make it clear, this is what your solution looks like:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9674904-5400-4651-ac05-409442f38e21

And here is how it is supposed to work:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74093914-476d-4381-9663-003dfcec2d2b

Of course I can create a **ScrollContainer** descendant that does what I want, but that was not necessary before 4.4 as we could just disable **follow_focus** and use our own logic to scroll. Now **follow_focus** is mandatory just to focus controls 'outside' the **ScrollContainer**.
**ScrollContainer** just lost useful flexibility which IMHO is a regression.

The use case is to allow the focus to quickly jump out of the visible range after switching.

Therefore, the requirement is: to be able to find descendant controls as focus outside the visible area of ​​the `ScrollContainer`, and to allow users to customize the scrolling logic.
